_comment: J41-qualified gVisor releases. Each entry binds expected sha512 per architecture for the binary at https://storage.googleapis.com/gvisor/releases/release/<release>/<arch>/runsc. Operators MUST NOT install runsc via secure-setup at a release not listed here; the binary-install path refuses unless `release` (env GVISOR_RELEASE, default: first entry) matches an entry AND the downloaded bytes' sha512 matches the recorded value. Adding a new entry requires (a) downloading runsc from upstream and computing sha512 per arch, (b) recording the qualification metadata below, (c) opening a PR.
_reference: Audit 2026-06-02 C6 + H5 + H6; first qualification 2026-06-03.
_security_model: The pin's load-bearing defense is the in-package sha512 — even if the GCS bucket / `latest` channel is compromised post-qualification, our pre-qualified sha512 (shipped INSIDE the npm tarball) catches the substitution and aborts the install. Upstream gVisor rotating /latest/ triggers an sha512 mismatch and forces re-qualification, which is intentional: a maintainer should sign off on every gVisor release we vouch for.
_gpg_fingerprint_source: https://gvisor.dev/archive.key (downloaded + dearmored on 2026-06-03; binary saved at assets/gvisor-archive-keyring.gpg)

releases._comment: Qualification 2026-06-03: ran sha512sum on the binary at /release/latest/<arch>/runsc as of GCS last-modified 2026-05-28 / etag 1d54d9eca06ce8e13463b25848bd7622. The sha512 binds the exact bytes; upstream rotation of /latest/ will cause a sha512 mismatch and force re-qualification.
